hook: SCP-342 is a transit ticket, and the whole file is about getting on board. It is long and told mostly through field reports and personal logs, so take the addenda in order; the escalation depends on it. Pay attention to who writes each section, because the voices change as the project wears down the people running it. Be ready for violent deaths along the way, among staff and bystanders alike.
whyItMatters: The premise is simple: an ordinary-looking ticket that, once used, commits its holder to a ride that never lets them off, conveyed through small wrongnesses in passengers, staff and weather. The doctor-clef tag might suggest Clef runs the show, but the real protagonist is the research team. It also reads as a long record of Foundation research failing, where each attempt to learn more mostly shows the team how little it controls.
thingsToNotice: The experiments escalate in method and in cost. The first D-class is last seen pounding on a bus window as it pulls away into mist; Agent Strahm then handcuffs himself to the next subject, beats passengers in frustration, and is later found comatose on a platform with an empty cuff marked by the prisoner's blood. When Strahm rides it himself, steadied by his friend Erin, a homeless man breaks Dr. Haber's neck, and Erin watches a spider-like thing in a conductor's cap wrap Strahm in a web and throw him out like nothing. Gunsther's hired driver refuses to stop even after his brakes fail and he runs over a little girl, until a sniper shoots him and a witness sees a second bus collect a burning corpse from the wreck; Gunsther admits the ticket may have been luring the team toward exactly that setup. Haber recovers from his broken neck only to be decapitated when his neck catches in a train door and the carriage passes a stone ledge, which ends the research. In the coda Gunsther's theatre ticket turns out to be SCP-342, he rides a taxi into an alley that dead-ends at a brick wall, and Clef's request to seal the file is undercut at once by the news that the ticket has broken its transit-only rule and some want testing reopened.
